survival_targets.method_en: finland / sweden / norway: NORDCAN age-standardised 5-year relative survival (%), as published. benchmark = mean of Sweden and Norway; gap_pp = Finland minus benchmark; lag_years = how many years ago the benchmark was at Finland's current level (interpolated between benchmark 13.85% at 2007 and 17.95% at 2012); gap_change_pp_per_decade = linear trend of the gap over 1990-1994..2020-2024 (negative = Finland falling further behind). Derived values computed in science/out/nordic_gap.

finland / sweden / norway: NORDCAN age-standardised 5-year relative survival (%), as published. benchmark = mean of Sweden and Norway; gap_pp = Finland minus benchmark; lag_years = how many years ago the benchmark was at Finland's current level (interpolated between benchmark 24.15% at 2012 and 32.95% at 2017); gap_change_pp_per_decade = linear trend of the gap over 1990-1994..2020-2024 (negative = Finland falling further behind). Derived values computed in science/out/nordic_gap.

mortality_trend.indicator: All-cancer mortality, both sexes, age-standardised (Finland 2014 standard population)
mortality_trend.note_en: The strategy says 'cancer mortality falls by 10 % (currently 13,300 people a year)' and gives no baseline year and no statement on whether the 10 % is counted in deaths or in the age-standardised rate. The registry's death counts round to 13,300 in 2022; 2022 is used here as the baseline (our reading, not the strategy's wording). In 2022 the rate was 207.51 and deaths 13,288; in 2024 203.53 and 13,490. Over the last ten years (2014-2024) the age-standardised rate changed -8.0 % while the number of deaths changed +11.6 % (ageing population). So a 10 % fall in the rate over ten years is close to the existing trend, while a 10 % fall in the number of deaths would need a break in the trend. Rates are per 100,000 person-years, standardised to the Finnish 2014 population; series from 2000.

treated_within_target.data_gap_en: No public source gives, for any cancer or any area, the share of cancer patients whose first treatment started within the target time. What was opened: (1) THL's 2016 guide defines the monitoring from the hospital care register (Hilmo) and says results will appear on THL.fi once data quality is acceptable; (2) THL's open specialist-care waiting-time reports are by specialty and procedure group only, so 'oncology' there means the oncology clinic's queue, not the cancer pathway; (3) the Cancer Registry's lung cancer report gives median days from diagnosis to first treatment by collaborative area (2018 to mid-2022), not by county, and we found no equivalent for pancreas or liver; (4) the strategy's roadmap schedules cancer-specific access times to be defined in 2026-2028. thl.fi itself could not be opened by script (bot challenge), so a publication there cannot be ruled out; a web search on 13 Nov 2026 found none.
treated_within_target.who_could_publish_en: THL, from Hilmo: referral date, diagnosis date and first treatment date by cancer and wellbeing services county, as the share within 42 days (the monitoring THL specified in Ohjaus 21/2016). The Finnish Cancer Registry could add time-to-treatment by county and for pancreas and liver to its quality reports (it already links Hilmo treatment dates for lung cancer). The wellbeing services counties and HUS hold the referral and treatment dates in their own patient systems; FICAN / the national cancer centre is named in the strategy as responsible for monitoring equal access.

notes_en: The registry's national totals are slightly larger than the sum of the 23 areas (at most 0.062 %, e.g. mortality pancreas male: 3251 nationally vs 3249 summed). The registry's table does not say why (cases without an area is our unverified reading). Shares of the national total computed from county counts will not sum to exactly 100 %.

Liver cancer deaths differ by source: the Cancer Registry counts 2472 deaths from liver cancer (C22) in 2020-2024, Statistics Finland's cause-of-death table 13u5 counts 3053 ('primary liver cancer, C22'), 19.0 % more. This file uses the registry's figures throughout (same source as incidence and survival). The reason for the difference was not verified from a source; do not mix the two sources in one comparison.

Incidence and mortality: Finnish Cancer Registry statistics application, 2020-2024, by wellbeing services county of residence (21 counties, Helsinki, Åland). Counts are five-year totals (per_year = count / 5). Rates are per 100,000 person-years, age-standardised to the Finnish 2014 population (crude_rate and asr_world, World standard, are kept on each rate row). Standardisation removes age-structure differences only: nothing is adjusted for smoking, alcohol, hepatitis, stage at diagnosis, comorbidity or socioeconomic position.
Site definitions (registry): lung = lung and trachea C33-34; pancreas = C25; liver = C22; all = all cancers together (C00-96, D09.0-1, D32-33, D41-43, D45-47, D76).

Small numbers: rows with fewer than 20 cases or deaths in the five years carry small_n: true (cancer, measure, sex: area ids): liver cases (all): 91; liver cases (female): 01, 18, 20, 91; liver cases (male): 91; liver deaths (all): 91; liver deaths (female): 01, 18, 20, 91; liver deaths (male): 91; pancreas cases (female): 91; pancreas deaths (female): 91. A rate built on under 20 events can double or halve by chance. The registry publishes no confidence intervals for the rates; with 100 events the 95 % range of a rate is still roughly +/- 20 % (Poisson), so look at n before reading a county difference in pancreas or liver rates. 2 counts are blank in the registry's table (value null, suppressed_n: true); the rate is still published.

Mortality is not a measure of care quality on its own: it mixes how many people get the cancer (incidence) with how long they live after diagnosis. Compare mortality_asr with incidence_asr for the same county before reading a high death rate as a care problem. No causal claims from county aggregates.

Survival is NOT published by county. The registry publishes age-standardised relative survival (1 to 5 years from diagnosis, 2022-2024) for the whole country, the five collaborative areas and Åland. County rows for survival_1y_pct / survival_5y_pct repeat the collaborative area's value and say so (level: collaborative_area); true-level rows are in collaborative_area[]. All-cancer survival is national only. Values the registry does not give (both sexes; collaborative areas without a value): lung 5-year: ALAND; pancreas 5-year: ALAND; liver 1-year: ALAND; liver 5-year: KYS, ALAND.

Survival targets use NORDCAN (5-year periods, by sex, countries only) because the strategy defines the target against NORDCAN. The registry's own national 5-year figures (in national[]) cover a different period and are not interchangeable with NORDCAN's.

The strategy's survival targets (+14 pp lung, +6 pp pancreas, +14 pp liver, 'from the 2023 level shown in NORDCAN', Nordic level = mean of Sweden and Norway) are not given by sex; strategy_target_pp repeats the same figure on the male and the female row.
